general.add: Insert Plenio as an instrument (VST3) on a new track.
general.tempo: Drop the Tempo map file at bar 1 and let your DAW take its tempo. If it does not, set the song's tempo by hand: the Click file shows where the bars fall.
general.stems: Activate Plenio's extra outputs (Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other, Rest): each stem plays on its own channel and leaves the main output. Or drag the Stems in.
general.midi: Drag the MIDI file onto an instrument track, or route Plenio's MIDI out (melody on channel 1, instrument line 2, chords 3).
general.audio: Drop every file at the project's start (bar 1): they all start there. If your DAW stretches audio to its tempo, switch that off for Plenio's audio: it keeps its own speed, and the tempo map makes the grid fit it.

daws.name: REAPER

table.tempo: from the file, or *Put on tracks*

daws.add: Insert › Virtual instrument on new track… › VST3i: Plenio (Plenio). When REAPER offers new tracks for Plenio's outputs (Build Routing Confirmation), say No: Put on tracks makes the song's tracks later.
daws.tempo: DAW tab › Put on tracks sets the project's tempo map from the take's bars. Or drop the Tempo map file at bar 1 and say yes when REAPER asks to import its tempo. Plenio keeps its own audio in the project in time (timebase Time): the grid moves onto the song, the song keeps its speed.
daws.stems: Put on tracks gives every stem a track of its own. Plenio's extra outputs can also be routed with the plug-in's I/O (pin connector) button.
daws.midi: Put on tracks adds Melody, Instrument Line and Chords as MIDI items, muted: put an instrument on their tracks to hear them.
daws.ara: Plenio ARA goes on an item: select it › Item › Take › Show FX chain for active take (Shift+E) › add Plenio ARA.
daws.audio: Space plays and stops REAPER, also while Plenio's window has the focus. Choose a take on the Song track (its take lane, or T): Plenio follows, and the other way round. The cover art becomes the icon of the song's tracks.

daws.name: Cubase and Nuendo

table.tempo: from the file (*File › Import › MIDI File*)

daws.tempo: File › Import › MIDI File… › the Tempo map file, with its tempo track. When you drag MIDI files in, the tempo comes along only with Preferences › MIDI › MIDI File › Ignore Master Track Events on Merge switched off.
daws.stems: Studio › VST Instruments (F11) › Plenio › activate the outputs Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other and Rest.
daws.midi: A MIDI track with its input set to Plenio: melody on channel 1, instrument line 2, chords 3.
daws.ara: Select the audio event › Audio › Extensions › Plenio ARA (Cubase Pro and Artist, Nuendo).
daws.audio: Audio on a musical time base only moves its start: Plenio's files start at bar 1 and keep their speed.

daws.name: Studio One

table.tempo: from the file (onto the tempo track)

daws.add: Browser › Instruments › drag Plenio into the arrangement.
daws.tempo: Drag the Tempo map file onto the tempo track: Studio One takes over its tempo.
daws.stems: In Plenio's instrument panel, switch on its outputs Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other and Rest: each becomes a channel in the mixer.
daws.midi: Drag the MIDI file onto an instrument track.
daws.ara: Right-click the audio event and choose Plenio ARA among its extensions.
daws.audio: Audio files without tempo information keep their speed: Plenio's carry none.

daws.name: Ableton Live
daws.add: Settings › Plug-Ins › Use VST3 Plug-in System Folders: on. Then Browser › Plug-Ins › VST3 › drag Plenio onto a MIDI track.
daws.tempo: Live takes no tempo from MIDI files: set Live's tempo to the song's (shown at the top of the song). For a song whose tempo drifts, the Click file shows where the bars fall.
daws.stems: An audio track per stem: Audio From › the Plenio track › Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other or Rest.
daws.midi: A MIDI track with MIDI From › the Plenio track: the melody, the instrument line and the chords.
daws.ara: Live has no ARA: Plenio ARA does not load there.
daws.audio: Switch Warp off on Plenio's audio clips: with Warp on, Live stretches them to its tempo.

daws.name: FL Studio
daws.add: Options › Manage plugins › Find plugins; then Channel rack › + › Plenio.
daws.tempo: Set the project's tempo to the song's (shown at the top of the song); the Click file shows where the bars fall.
daws.stems: Plenio's wrapper › Processing (the gear) › send Plenio's outputs to mixer tracks of their own.
daws.midi: Drag the MIDI file onto the playlist, or into another instrument's piano roll.
daws.audio: Audio clips keep their speed as long as their time-stretching stays off.

daws.name: Bitwig Studio
daws.add: Browser › Plug-ins › drag Plenio onto an instrument track.
daws.tempo: Set Bitwig's tempo to the song's (shown at the top of the song); the Click file shows where the bars fall.
daws.stems: Plenio's extra outputs show as chains of the device: add the chains Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other and Rest.
daws.midi: A Note Receiver on another track, listening to the Plenio track.
daws.audio: If Bitwig stretches Plenio's audio to its tempo, switch the clip's time-stretching off in the Inspector.

daws.name: Cakewalk and Sonar

table.tempo: from the file, else by hand

daws.add: Insert › Soft Synth › Plenio, as an instrument track.
daws.tempo: Import the Tempo map file (File › Import › MIDI); if the tempo does not come along, set it by hand (the Click file helps).
daws.stems: Synth Rack › Plenio › give its outputs Vocals, Drums, Bass, Other and Rest tracks of their own.
daws.midi: Drag the MIDI file onto a MIDI track.
daws.ara: Right-click the audio clip › Region FX › Plenio ARA.

daws.name: Logic Pro
daws.unsupported: Logic Pro loads Audio Units only: Plenio VST3 does not run in Logic. Plenio's files work there all the same: make the song in another DAW, or drag the files from the song's folder.

daws.name: Pro Tools
daws.unsupported: Pro Tools loads AAX plug-ins only: Plenio VST3 does not run in Pro Tools. Its files work there all the same: drag them in from the song's folder.
